answers.core:
RDShaderSPIRV is a core type (correct?), and it's difficult and redundant to link another C++ extension or library as an intermediary to "query" about a SPIRV shader representation.

It's important that core should NOT include the interpretation and validations of this data. User projects and needs are too diverse for a one-size-fits-all approach in core, but having just the reflection data available for engine users is empowering us to build shader-first workflows instead of building RD-script-first, then shader, then back to script, then back to editing the shader workflows, dozens of times over.
answers.workaround: There's no workaround because there is no way of inspecting what is in a RDShaderSPIRV.

title: Expose SPIRV-Cross Reflection Data in RDShaderSPIRV
